''Moved from [[terki]]''

*[[User:Mark Shoulson|.mark.]]:
**An odd feature of Lojban is that you actually have to use '''[[zoi]]'''-quotes to talk about some [[rafsi]].  I can say '''zo xuk. rafsi zo xruki''' and '''zo li'u [[rafsi]] zo litru''', but I have to say '''[[zoi]] .ly. cpi .ly. rafsi zo cipni''', since '''cpi-''' isn't a valid Lojban word of any sort. I suppose the same is true of '''-lan-''' for '''lanme''', but for less meaningful reasons.

See [[the Book]], chapter 19, section 10, example 10.5.

*Yuck. I foresee one change that will happen in Lojban usage - '''zo cpi''' would become acceptable even if it doesn't parse. Otherwise how can you fill the x1 of '''[[rafsi|rafsi]]''' in a reasonable way?
**[[User:Mark Shoulson|.mark.]]:
***Well, you can use ''[[zoi|zoi]]'', like I did above.  That's "reasonable"... but only barely, I'll admit.  '''-lan-''' is a harder one to remember, since it fails legality for more subtle reasons (I personally believe we should have abolished the nonsense about no '''la'''/'''lai'''/'''doi''' in [[cmevla]] and just required a mandatory pause before as well as after in all settings.)
****[[rab.spir|rab.spir]]:
*****I don't think that '''zo .cpi.''', with pauses before and after, would ever be ambiguous. Could this be considered an extremely minor extension to the word resolution algorithm?
******Adam:
*******I like using '''cy.py.ibu''' or '''la me cy.py.ibu''' to refer to rafsi. It solves the CCV problem and also treats all rafsi identically, thus solving the problem of call the word '''li'u''' a rafsi and not a cmavo.
********mark:
********* '''cy.py.ibu''' is a variable, a pro-sumti referring to something called CPI.  '''la me cy.py.ibu''' is no better.  You need '''me'o cy.py.ibu''', believe it or not.  I'm told that's the way to refer to actual letters.
**********phma:
***********I use '''[[zoi]]''' for all rafsi. '''zo li'u''' is the word that is used to close a quotation, not the fragment of a word that is the rafsi of '''litru'''.
*raphael:
**Actually, there is still no word resolution [[WordResolutionAlgorithm|Algorithm]]. And current lexers can easily be modified to treat anything delimited by pauses after '''zo''' correctly.
***Adam:
****There is non-debugged and non-baselined WordResolutionAlgorithm at http://www.lojban.org/files/software/BRKWORDS.TXT It would reject '''cpi''', though with a pause both before and after it couldn't be mistake as a part of another word.
